conventions.convention: Velocity uses SI units; reduced pressure is p = P/ρ₀ for fixed positive constant density, and ν is positive kinematic viscosity. Smoothness includes continuous right-hand extensions of all derivatives to t = 0.

Fefferman alternatives A and C require uniformly bounded whole-space energy. Alternatives B and D require periodic velocity and smooth pressure, without requiring periodic pressure or a separate uniform energy bound.

Ω is a nonempty open subset of R²; I and Θ are nonempty open intervals, with Θ positive and dimensionless. U,L > 0 are fixed, ν(θ) = UL/θ, and u: Ω × I × Θ → R² is continuously differentiable. The four input coordinates are x,y,t,θ; output components contribute no input axes.

load_bearing.statement: For the stated continuously differentiable family u: Ω × I × Θ → R² on nonempty open factors, sampling in x,y,t,θ gives four independent input axes. Fixing θ leaves two spatial coordinates and one time coordinate; Reynolds number indexes settings, and the two velocity components are outputs.
